Losing our first big customer was the best thing that ever happened to Ledgerline.

Let me explain.

5 months in, they walked away. It stung. A lot.

Failure isn't the opposite of success. It's part of it.

The reason they left: they had heavily customized their NetSuite instance, and we only supported standard fields. We weren't meeting them where they were.

So we listened, we learned, and we built.

We spent 6 weeks adding support for custom fields. It changed how we think about our customers, not just what we ship.

Today, we serve 38 customers. 11 of them rely on custom fields.

Your biggest setback can become your biggest breakthrough. Lean into the hard feedback. Your customers are telling you what to build, you just have to listen.

What's a loss that shaped your company?

#Startups #SaaS #Leadership #CustomerSuccess #Growth

1,200 repositories.

When we launched Patchwork CI, we promised it would always be free for open source. People told us we were crazy. How would we make money?

Today we run on 1,200 repositories. About 900 of them are open source.

Here's what got me: across all those repos, 1 in 7 CI failures turned out to be a flaky test. One in seven. Think about how many hours you've burned on red builds that were never real failures.

Open source gave us more than users. It gave us data, feedback, and a community. Our most-requested feature, GitLab support, came straight from OSS maintainers. We shipped it on November 12.

Giving back isn't charity. It's strategy.

#OpenSource #DevOps #CI #DeveloperExperience #BuildInPublic

1,000 families.

14 months ago, Pebble Pantry was nothing more than a note on my phone. I wrote it down on maternity leave, running on no sleep, with nothing in the fridge at 7pm and no plan for dinner.

So to every mum and dad who mentioned us in a group chat, thank you. This exists because you passed it along.

And if you're a founder working with almost nothing: keep at it. The people around you will do more than any budget could.

#Startups #Portugal #Parenting #FemaleFounders #Gratitude

Our app was beautiful. Nobody used it.

We launched Rotaship with a sleek, modern mobile app and figured restaurant staff would take to it right away.

The numbers showed otherwise. In the first month, just 12% of staff opened it.

That stung, but it taught us something. The app wasn't fixing their problem. It was a new problem on top of the old one.

Restaurant teams already have their tool of choice: WhatsApp. They weren't going to switch for us.

So in 2025 we made the hard decision to move the whole product into WhatsApp.

It worked. We now serve 140 outlets, and the median reply time to shift messages is under 20 minutes.

The lesson: go to your users, don't wait for them to come to you.

Letting go of the thing you love can be the best product decision you make.

#ProductManagement #Indonesia #StartupLessons #UserExperience

We're hiring.

If you want to make an impact and grow with us, apply via the link in the comments.

We stopped billing by the hour, and we're never going back.

Hourly rates were the default when we launched Fernway Studio, so that's what we used.

4 of our first 6 projects blew past budget. Clients were frustrated, we were frustrated, and trust started slipping away.

In 2024 we made the call to charge a flat KES 450,000 per Shopify store. That's it.

Everything shifted after that. Clients know the price upfront, we have a reason to work efficiently instead of dragging things out, and the relationship rests on trust rather than timesheets.

We've launched 31 stores since the switch. Just 2 ran past our 6-week timeline.

A price is a promise, not just a number.

Founders, how do you set your prices? Tell me in the comments.

I spent 11 years working in a vet clinic before quitting. What pushed me out was hard to watch.

I loved the work itself. But too many animals came in so frightened that sedation was the only way we could get through an examination.

There had to be another option, I kept thinking.

In 2023 I started Doorstep Vet. The idea: give pets the same quality of care, but at home, where they already feel safe.

We now have 4 vets on the team, doing roughly 30 home visits a week. Each visit reminds me why I left the clinic.

The pets are calmer. The owners are happier. The medicine is better.

Sometimes following your heart is the bravest choice you can make.
